title: What is millennial burnout
paragraphs: Do you often feel stressed? Does the pace of life make you feel like you're continually on the go or at the end of your rope? Are you often so wiped out by work that you struggle to switch off? And are you a member of the millennial generation, who, according to the Pew Research Center, were born between 1981 and 1996? If your answer to these questions is 'yes', maybe you suffer from 'millennial burnout'.

Millennial burnout is a term first popularised by BuzzFeed writer Anne Helen Petersen. Unlike 'regular' burnout, which leaves sufferers feeling physically and emotionally frazzled, run into the ground and overwhelmed, millennial burnout also adds, among other things, 'errand paralysis'. This is when minor tasks, such as cleaning the car, or sending a parcel in the mail, feel impossible. "It's not as if I were slacking in the rest of my life," she wrote. "But when it came to the stuff that wouldn't make my job easier or my work better, I avoided it." So it doesn't get done, which leads to a backlog of tasks and feelings of shame.

In the UK, 74% of us feel so stressed that we are coming apart at the seams, mentalhealth.org reports. So why are millennials tearing their hair out? Millennials feel their problems are 'exacerbated by social media, because of the constant pressure to be living up to your best life,' British psychotherapist Beverly Hills told the BBC. This pressure is made worse when the definition of 'success' seems to have changed. It used to be about earning money, but now it's things like being passionate about work, being super-healthy, holidaying and having amazing experiences, etc. That's a lot to have on your plate and the 'failure' to cope leaves many feeling guilty, ashamed and at their wits' end.

However, the concept of millennial burnout has not gone unchallenged. Many have said that it's merely a form of entitled laziness or the result of poor choices – for example, trying to do too much. After all, as psychoanalyst Josh Cohen writes for NBC, this isn't the first generation to suffer from overwork and exhaustion, nor is it the first to have to adapt to new forms of technology and culture. Could the answer simply be that millennial ambition reaches too far?

vocabulary.entry: on the go /ɒn ðə ɡəʊ/ 忙个不停；四处奔波
vocabulary.example: She's always on the go from morning till night.
vocabulary.translation: 她总是从早到晚忙个不停。

vocabulary.term: at the end of one's rope
vocabulary.entry: at the end of one's rope /æt ði end ɒv wʌnz rəʊp/ 山穷水尽；走投无路
vocabulary.example: After losing his job, he felt at the end of his rope.
vocabulary.translation: 失业后，他感到走投无路。

vocabulary.entry: wiped out /waɪpt aʊt/ 筋疲力尽的
vocabulary.example: I was completely wiped out after the long hike.
vocabulary.translation: 长途徒步旅行后，我已经筋疲力尽了。

vocabulary.entry: switch off /swɪtʃ ɒf/ 放松；不再操心
vocabulary.example: I find it hard to switch off after a busy day at work.
vocabulary.translation: 忙碌的一天工作结束后，我很难放松下来。

vocabulary.entry: millennial burnout /mɪˈleniəl ˈbɜːnaʊt/ 千禧一代倦怠症
vocabulary.example: Many young people are suffering from millennial burnout due to work pressure.
vocabulary.translation: 许多年轻人因工作压力而患上了千禧一代倦怠症。

vocabulary.entry: popularise /ˈpɒpjələraɪz/ v. 推广；使普及
vocabulary.example: The singer helped popularise this style of music.
vocabulary.translation: 这位歌手助力推广了这种音乐风格。

vocabulary.entry: frazzled /ˈfræzld/ adj. 疲惫不堪的；心力交瘁的
vocabulary.example: She looked frazzled after dealing with the problem all day.
vocabulary.translation: 一整天处理这个问题后，她看上去疲惫不堪。

vocabulary.entry: run into the ground /rʌn ˈɪntu ðə ɡraʊnd/ 使精疲力竭；耗尽心力
vocabulary.example: Overworking has run him into the ground.
vocabulary.translation: 超负荷工作让他心力交瘁。

vocabulary.entry: overwhelmed /ˌəʊvəˈwelmd/ adj. 不堪重负的；不知所措的
vocabulary.example: She felt overwhelmed by the amount of work.
vocabulary.translation: 面对堆积如山的工作，她感到不堪重负。

vocabulary.entry: errand paralysis /ˈerənd pəˈræləsɪs/ 琐事瘫痪症
vocabulary.example: Errand paralysis makes even small tasks seem impossible to finish.
vocabulary.translation: 琐事瘫痪症会让哪怕是微小的任务，都显得难以完成。

vocabulary.entry: slack /slæk/ v. 偷懒；懈怠
vocabulary.example: Don't slack off when the boss is away.
vocabulary.translation: 老板不在的时候不要偷懒。

vocabulary.entry: backlog /ˈbæklɒɡ/ n. 积压的工作；待办事项
vocabulary.example: The company has a backlog of orders to process.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司有一大批积压的订单需要处理。

vocabulary.entry: come apart at the seams /kʌm əˈpɑːt æt ðə siːmz/ 濒临崩溃；四分五裂
vocabulary.example: The team came apart at the seams after losing the final.
vocabulary.translation: 输掉决赛后，这支队伍濒临解散。

vocabulary.entry: tear one's hair out /teə wʌnz heə aʊt/ 焦虑抓狂；极度烦恼
vocabulary.example: He was tearing his hair out over the delay of the project.
vocabulary.translation: 因为项目延期，他焦虑得抓狂。

vocabulary.entry: exacerbate /ɪɡˈzæsəbeɪt/ v. 使恶化；加剧
vocabulary.example: The heavy rain exacerbated the flood situation.
vocabulary.translation: 暴雨加剧了洪涝灾情。

vocabulary.entry: live up to /lɪv ʌp tu/ 达到；不辜负（期望）
vocabulary.example: She tried her best to live up to her parents' expectations.
vocabulary.translation: 她尽全力不辜负父母的期望。

vocabulary.term: have a lot on one's plate
vocabulary.entry: have a lot on one's plate /hæv ə lɒt ɒn wʌnz pleɪt/ 有很多事情要处理
vocabulary.example: I can't take on more work; I already have a lot on my plate.
vocabulary.translation: 我不能再承担更多工作了，我手头已经有很多事要做。

vocabulary.entry: at one's wits' end /æt wʌnz wɪts end/ 手足无措；黔驴技穷
vocabulary.example: The teacher was at her wits' end with the naughty student.
vocabulary.translation: 面对这个调皮的学生，老师已经手足无措了。

vocabulary.entry: unchallenged /ʌnˈtʃælɪndʒd/ adj. 未受质疑的；未被挑战的
vocabulary.example: His authority remained unchallenged for many years.
vocabulary.translation: 多年来，他的权威一直未受到质疑。

vocabulary.entry: entitled /ɪnˈtaɪtld/ adj. 自以为有权的；恃宠而骄的
vocabulary.example: Some people think the younger generation is too entitled.
vocabulary.translation: 有些人认为年轻一代过于恃宠而骄。

vocabulary.entry: adapt to /əˈdæpt tu/ 适应
vocabulary.example: It takes time to adapt to a new environment.
vocabulary.translation: 适应新环境需要时间。

vocabulary.entry: reach too far /riːtʃ tuː fɑː/ 野心过大；不自量力
vocabulary.example: His plan to expand the business quickly reached too far.
vocabulary.translation: 他想要快速扩张业务的计划野心太大了。

sentences.chinese: 你经常感到“压力山大”吗？

sentences.chinese: 快节奏的生活是否让你觉得自己一直在奔波忙碌，或是陷入了绝望的境地？

sentences.english: Unlike 'regular' burnout, which leaves sufferers feeling physically and emotionally frazzled, run into the ground and overwhelmed, millennial burnout also adds, among other things, 'errand paralysis'.
sentences.chinese: 普通倦怠症会让患者身心俱疲、心力交瘁、不堪重负，而千禧一代倦怠症除此之外，还会引发一种“琐事瘫痪症”。

sentences.chinese: 她在文中写道：“我不会在生活其他方面偷懒，但遇到那些没法让我的工作更轻松、表现更出色的事情时，我就会刻意回避。”

sentences.english: So it doesn't get done, which leads to a backlog of tasks and feelings of shame.
sentences.chinese: 这些事就此被搁置，久而久之就会堆积成山，进而让人产生愧疚感。

sentences.english: In the UK, 74% of us feel so stressed that we are coming apart at the seams, mentalhealth.org reports.
sentences.chinese: 心理健康组织的报告显示，在英国，有74%的人因为压力过大而濒临崩溃。

sentences.english: So why are millennials tearing their hair out?
sentences.chinese: 那么，为什么千禧一代会如此焦虑抓狂呢？

sentences.english: Millennials feel their problems are 'exacerbated by social media, because of the constant pressure to be living up to your best life,' British psychotherapist Beverly Hills told the BBC.
sentences.chinese: 英国心理治疗师贝弗莉·希尔斯在接受英国广播公司采访时表示，千禧一代的问题“因社交媒体而加剧，因为他们时刻都承受着要活出完美人生的压力”。

sentences.english: This pressure is made worse when the definition of 'success' seems to have changed.
sentences.chinese: 而“成功”的定义似乎也发生了改变，这让他们的压力雪上加霜。

sentences.english: It used to be about earning money, but now it's things like being passionate about work, being super-healthy, holidaying and having amazing experiences, etc.
sentences.chinese: 过去，成功的标准是赚钱，但如今，成功被定义为热爱工作、拥有极佳的健康状态、频繁度假以及拥有丰富多彩的人生体验等。

sentences.english: That's a lot to have on your plate and the 'failure' to cope leaves many feeling guilty, ashamed and at their wits' end.
sentences.chinese: 要兼顾这么多事情实属不易，一旦无法做到，很多人就会陷入愧疚、羞耻与手足无措的情绪中。

sentences.english: However, the concept of millennial burnout has not gone unchallenged.
sentences.chinese: 不过，“千禧一代倦怠症”这个概念也并非毫无争议。

sentences.english: Many have said that it's merely a form of entitled laziness or the result of poor choices – for example, trying to do too much.
sentences.chinese: 很多人认为，这不过是一种恃宠而骄的懒惰，或是不当选择的后果，比如想要做太多事情。

sentences.english: After all, as psychoanalyst Josh Cohen writes for NBC, this isn't the first generation to suffer from overwork and exhaustion, nor is it the first to have to adapt to new forms of technology and culture.
sentences.chinese: 毕竟，正如精神分析师乔希·科恩在为美国全国广播公司撰稿时所写的那样，这并非第一代遭受过度劳累和疲惫之苦的人，也不是第一代必须去适应新技术、新文化的群体。

sentences.english: Could the answer simply be that millennial ambition reaches too far?
sentences.chinese: 答案可能非常简单——千禧一代想要的太多了？
